title: Liquidity: when can the client get money back?
objectives: State the exit route for MF, PMS, Cat I & II and Cat III.
Explain drawdowns and why early exit is usually impossible for Cat I & II.
body_md:
MF: usually within a few working days of redemption. PMS: can exit anytime; exit loads may apply in the first three years; securities may be sold or transferred back. Category I & II AIF: money is typically drawn down in stages and returned as investments are exited, often over 5–8+ years. Early exit is usually not possible. Category III AIF: depends on the scheme; some offer periodic redemptions.

> **Talk-track:** “Here's what each option would cost you in rupees, how long your money is locked, and how it's taxed. Let's compare before you decide.”
example: Cat I & II AIF: commitment drawn in stages; money returned as investments are exited over 5–8+ years — early exit usually not possible.
say: Money returns as investments are exited.
Early exit is usually not possible for Cat I & II.
never: Cat II AIFs can be exited any business day.
